newsitem.title: UK: ICCO sees world 96/97 cocoa deficit at 225,000 T.
newsitem.headline: ICCO sees world 96/97 cocoa deficit at 225,000 T.

text.p: The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) on Monday forecast a world 96/97 cocoa defict of 225,000 tonnes against a surplus of 120,000 tonnes in the 95/96 season, ICCO delegates said.
Delegates said the ICCO put world 96/97 output at 2.485 million tonnes and consumption at 2.71 million tonnes.
The ICCO on Monday revised upwards its 95/96 world cocoa surplus to 120,000 tonnes from 20,000 tonnes in its previous forecast in June.
The increase in world output reflects higher output from the Ivory Coast.
The ICCO now put total output for 95/96 at 2.831 million tonnes against 2.731 million tonnes.
It put world stocks-to-grinding ratio at 42 percent at end-1996/97 season and 51 percent at end 95/96.
The Ivorian crop could reach 950,000 tonnes for the coming season, down from 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96, said the delegates.
